History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
24-year-old woman with 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache, nausea, and subjective fever/diaphoresis; no vomiting or urinary pain; advised to attend same-day face-to-face GP review to rule out pregnancy and other causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Constant dull ache below the umbilicus with associated nausea and feeling hot/sweaty for the past 2 days.  
• Onset/progression: Gradual onset 2 days ago; symptoms persistent and worsening discomfort.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Polyuria (increased frequency) without dysuria, urgency, foul odor, or suprapubic pain.  
  – Mild pink coloration noted in urine over the last couple of days; patient is due for her period soon (LMP ~3 weeks ago).  
  – No vomiting, no diarrhoea, no vaginal discharge, no light-headedness/fainting.  
• Recent bowel pattern: Constipation one week ago, now resolved; passed stool yesterday; currently normal bowel motions.  
• Gynecologic/sexual history: Sexually active with one partner; etonogestrel implant (Implanon) in situ; uncertain pregnancy risk but believes low; last menstrual period ~3 weeks ago; mild spotting/pink urine last few days.  
• Review of systems: No chest pain, shortness of breath, or other systemic complaints reported.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Etonogestrel contraceptive implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies:
• Amoxicillin – allergy (reaction details not specified).

Social History:
• Lives with boyfriend.  
• Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol and other substance use not discussed.

Family History:
• Brother with type 1 diabetes.  
• Otherwise non-contributory per patient.

Physical Examination:
(Not performed during video consultation; no vitals documented.)

Investigations:
• None performed during call.  
• Plan to perform pregnancy test and further examinations/laboratory tests at face-to-face GP visit.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Lower-abdominal pain with nausea; differential includes constipation, urinary tract pathology, gynecologic causes (including pregnancy/ectopic).  
  – Arrange same-day in-person GP assessment for abdominal and pelvic examination.  
  – Urgent urine pregnancy test; consider serum β-hCG if indicated.  
  – Urinalysis and possible urine culture.  
  – Further labs or imaging as guided by examination findings.

Issue 2: Possible low-grade fever/hyperthermia.  
  – Check temperature and vital signs at in-person visit.  
  – Monitor for escalation (rigors, high fever).

Issue 3: Safety-netting.  
  – Advise patient to seek urgent care (ED/GP) if pain intensifies, develops light-headedness, true haematuria, heavy vaginal bleeding, vomiting, or any other concerning symptoms before scheduled review.

General Plan items:  
  – Provide patient education regarding symptom monitoring and when to seek help.  
  – Follow-up appointment after initial work-up or sooner if condition changes.

Quality checks:

● Missing/expected: Physical examination, vital signs, full medication reconciliation, detailed allergy reaction, alcohol use history.  
● Internal conflicts: Doctor references “three days” of symptoms while patient later confirms “last two days” – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear, no major audio issues; minimal overlapping speech.
